utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume our hearing. Usher, have the accused brought in, please. (Accused enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First, I would like to be sure that the interpreters are ready. First of all, I would like to ask whether everybody hears me. Mr. Blaskic, do you hear me? GENERAL BLASKIC: Good morning, your Honour, Mr. President. I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do the Defence hear, my assistants, my colleagues hear me? So we can begin at the point where we left off, that is the examination was completed and I think we now have to begin the cross-examination of the Prosecutor's witness. Mr. Prosecutor, do you have a comment you would like to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, just before we begin with Mr. Leach, I have copies in French of Prosecutor's Exhibit 79. They were not available when they were tendered. I have copies for the court. At this point I would like to offer them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Perhaps we could have your witness brought in. Mr. Harmon, before the cross-examination begins, it will be Mr. Nobilo or Mr. Hayman? It's Mr. Hayman. (Documents handed).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps the usher could have the witness brought in. (Witness enters court).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Simon Leach, good morning. Do you hear me now, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You hear me. Fine. Without any further delay we can go forward. Mr. Hayman, you can begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour and good morning, your Honours, counsel and Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are the lead investigator in this matter for the office of the Tribunal of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you held that position as lead investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came to the Office of the Prosecutor in October 1994, actually took up the position mid-November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you held that position for roughly a year before the indictment was sought and obtained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've held it at all times since?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the lead investigator are you familiar with the status of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you the custodian of the physical evidence in the possession of the office of the Tribunal Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There's an evidence unit, which takes possession of any articles that are taken by any investigator. Within any investigative team there are large numbers of investigative teams. So the evidence of the custodian is outside the investigative unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you and other investigators working under you check evidence with the custodian in essence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would direct what goes into that vault or secure location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many investigators, investigative assistants or analysts do you have on your team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Currently we have five investigators and then we have support staff of a research assistant, legal analysts, military analysts, possibly numbering 14 in total, 14 to 16. Depending on what project is being dealt with depends on which the team or departments within the Office of the Prosecutor one would go to for extra resources or assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does 14 or 15 include the five investigators or the other categories?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that includes the five investigators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you have testified that the HVO or HVO forces attacked various villages on 16th April and/or on subsequent days in 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Villages in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you or does your office possess a single written order of Tihomir Blaskic directing any attack on a civilian target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What order is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have it in my possession with me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I am going to object, your Honour. I think this is outside the scope of the examination. Mr. Leach testified about the introduction of physical exhibits. He did not testify beyond that and he did not testify about other exhibits that were not tendered before this court. This is a wide-ranging cross-examination and I would object to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: May I be heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In general I would prefer that objections be made either by the Defence or the Prosecution in respect of very, very significant objectives. I said this to Mr. Hayman the other day. The cross-examination has only begun and this Trial Chamber has judges, no jury. They know how to distinguish what is part of the cross-examination and what is not part of that cross-examination. Therefore, Mr. Hayman, you can go on. Proceed, please, but try to remain within the context of what Mr. Simon Leach has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. What written order of Tihomir Blaskic do you or your office possess that directs an attack on a civilian target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have the order in my possession with me in front of me. Whether it would be classed as a document which directs an attack on a civilian target, I would have to read the text. It may direct an attack on or an offensive operation. Again the phrase "attack" may not be contained in the documents, but it may describe an offensive operation against a location rather than a direct: "Go and attack".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this order relate to 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there's no such order in your or your office's possession with respect to the events surrounding 16th April 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards to an attack, I'm not aware of an order of that kind, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do possess written orders from my client, do you not, directing that HVO soldiers not harm civilians and not harm civilian property, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe you have copies of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Exhibit 29D be placed before the witness? (Handed.) This is a small map of the Kiseljak area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have identified various villages or hamlets within this area; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to -- one moment. (Pause.) Can you estimate for us how far Gomionica is from Behrici? Do you see those two locations on the map? Perhaps you might put it on the ELMO, if that's convenient, and we can all follow along. Currently you are pointing to Behrici; is that right, or you are pointing in between the two villages I mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you estimate this is under 1,000 metres between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 1,000 metres, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does one village or hamlet end and the next begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In relation to both this location and other locations I have testified about it is sometimes quite difficult to say one village starts here, ends here, there's a break in the road and then the next village starts. The people who lived in the villages are the people who can be very specific about where a village starts and where a village ends and where the next village closest to it would start.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the nature of, well, if you are on the other side of the creek you are in Gomionica but this side of the creek is Behrici, this kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no sign as you leave the village of Behrici, leaving the village of Behrici, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because even on foot in a few minutes you are in the next hamlet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that same observation apply, for example, with respect to Svinjarevo and Behrici and they are extraordinary close and approximate in territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In relation to Gomionica and Behrici, yes, because I know from being there as you walk between middle Gomionica and upper Gomionica, you have to take a track to the left to walk into Behrici. From recollection Svinjarevo would be in line of sight from Behrici but I don't think there is a defined track or pathway or road to walk from, for example, Behrici to Svinjarevo. Certainly I saw no indication of a road we could use. You would have to drive back down through Gomionica to the main highway, travel to Busovaca for 1.5 or 2 kms and then travel back to Svinjarevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would go back to the road for 1,000 metres or two and then you would be in the Svinjarevo area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there was gunfire in any of these villages stretching from Visnjica to Svinjarevo, would you likely hear that gunfire in other villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you described the distance from the Kiseljak Barracks to various villages in the Kiseljak Municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that Tihomir Blaskic maintained a headquarters with a headquarters or command staff in the Kiseljak Barracks at any time material to this indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding is this, your Honours, that approximately May 1992 General Blaskic had recently arrived in Central Bosnia via Vienna and Tuzla and had responsibility for the HVO in Kiseljak. Subsequent to that he was given the post of commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and established the main headquarters at the Hotel Vitez in Vitez and he had a subordinate brigade commander and brigade battalions at the HVO headquarters at the barracks in Kiseljak. I cannot say, I do not know whether or not he had a command staff at Kiseljak. It is my understanding that he most certainly had a command staff at Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So based on what you have just said your understanding then, to summarise, is at some point close in time to May 1992 if Tihomir Blaskic ever had a headquarters in Kiseljak Barracks, that headquarters moved to the Hotel Vitez; correct? It moved to the Vitez area. Let me state it that way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's sometimes difficult for me to qualify and say that he didn't have command staff at Kiseljak. I'm aware that when he was involved in negotiations which were brokered, I think, by UNPROFOR and possibly the European Community monitoring mission, that those negotiations could and did take place in Kiseljak, and therefore material I have seen would indicate that the General may be perceived to have had a headquarters at Kiseljak as well, but the General would know himself better than I .

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those meetings and discussions in 1992 or 1993, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were certainly some in 1993, possibly 1992. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it you're not able to give any testimony on whether or not Tihomir Blaskic maintained a headquarters in Kiseljak Barracks at any time approximate to the dates of the so-called attacks you have described on the villages in the municipality of Kiseljak as set forth in Exhibit 29D; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I would say is that he had a subordinate command at that location that was subordinate to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that different from having a command headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you have described what he had or what existed at Kiseljak Barracks as a headquarters of Tihomir Blaskic. Is it now your testimony that you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that my understanding is that he had a headquarters at Kiseljak Barracks. He was there regularly. I think possibly because at the initial stages of UNPROFOR's arrival in Bosnia as a whole -- UNPROFOR initially -- the main Bosnia-Herzegovina command of UNPROFOR was stationed at Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you use headquarters in that sense, what do you mean by headquarters? Do you mean a conference room where he was sometimes seen or do you mean something more than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I meant something more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a command or headquarters staff at Kiseljak barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked by Mr. Harmon whether after 16th April 1993 the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina cut the main road between Kacuni and Bilalovic. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer was "yes"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The main road you referred to is also the main road or artery between Kiseljak and Busovaca; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And similarly to get from Kiseljak to Vitez, you would have to take that same road through Busovaca and on up to Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not an expert of every road in Central Bosnia, your Honours. It is my understanding that both parties, both the Armija of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO, would have the ability to travel from point A, for example, in Busovaca to point B in Kiseljak but using mountain routes, mountain paths, if they had a suitable 4-wheel drive vehicle, etc., but the main highway would be the one been Kiseljak and Busovaca, which could be cut off to normal routes by certain factions at certain locations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Exhibit 29C, your Honour, be placed before the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps D11 could be gathered so as to conserve time as the next exhibit to be shown to the witness. (Handed.) Could you put 29C on the ELMO and show us the road of which we are discussing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The road from?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The road from Vitez to Busovaca, then on to Kiseljak, although Kiseljak does not appear on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you are indicating the town of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Down towards Busovaca or Kiseljak, you would go in an easterly, south easterly direction. Would you trace that? Thank you. Then you move to the map to the left. You reach the Busovaca T-junction here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you turn right, if you proceed down on the road, that takes us to Busovaca; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you continue on down the road and tell us when you come to Kacuni,, please, if it's on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are now indicating the town of Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could continue on down to the end of the map showing this map going off the map, and then replace this map, if you would, with Exhibit 29D, if you still have it. Perhaps you could start with Kacuni, pick up the same road, in other words, with Kacuni on 29D. You are pointing to Kacuni now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continue down the route to the south, south-east, and let us know when you come to Bilalovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How are you indicating Bilalovic on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you continue down this road it takes you to Kiseljak; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that this road was cut at Kacuni in the latter half of January 1997 by forces of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The latter half of January, beginning of February, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately on or about January 23rd, 1993, wasn't this road cut in the area of Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That may be the exact date, but I would have to check records to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That road was never reopened, that is it was never taken back by the HVO in the course of the entire war, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware that that's the case, but you may be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that from January 23rd, 1993, the only way that Tihomir Blaskic could pass on this road was in a UN vehicle, being escorted for purposes of cease-fires or other means, which may have been occurring in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm aware that General Blaskic was often, as were members of the Bosnian army, in armoured personnel carriers, in order to get either side through certain checkpoints or confrontation lines as they developed. However, as I said earlier, that does not necessarily mean that one could not get from, for example, Vitez to Busovaca without avoiding a HB checkpoint and likewise one could possibly, using mountain roads, travel from Busovaca to Kiseljak. I am not an expert, but that is what I'm led to believe was the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information that you can provide this Tribunal that after January 23rd, 1993 Tihomir Blaskic ever travelled on the road we have been discussing through the Kacuni/Bilalovic portion, in any manner other than a UN vehicle? Do you have any other information to suggest to the contrary that you can provide this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not with me. I would have to check records but that may be -- you may be accurate that he did not without an UNPROFOR escort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you do, you don't have it in your mind; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information you can provide this Tribunal that would confirm that Tihomir Blaskic ever trekked across the mountains after January 23rd, 1993 to try to get to Kiseljak from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May Exhibit D/11 be placed before the witness and if he could place it on the ELMO, please. I think you may have it. It is the excerpts from Lord Owen's book, "Balkan Odyssey". If you would open the package, turn to the last page and there is a map on the last page. If you would place that on the ELMO, that would be very helpful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 363.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. If the camera could zoom in on the Vitez and Kiseljak pockets, please. A little bit more, please. That's plenty. If you could move the map down a little, Mr. Leach. Yes, perfect. Mr. Leach, does this map illustrate the fact that this road, at least the portion between Kacuni and Bilalovic, was cut and was not held by the HVO? Do you see a gap between two shaded portions, one around Vitez and the other around Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this consistent with your understanding that there was, if you will, a Vitez enclave, a surrounded enclave, held by the HVO and similarly another surrounded enclave held by the HVO to the south-east in and around Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I would describe as enclaves. Whether this document was designed to show how people could travel on the roads, I'm not so sure that's an accurate portrayal how one could travel from A to B. Certainly I know that, for example, the city of Prozor, which is not on this map, to the south-west of Vitez and Kiseljak, that the HVO were building a road to connect Prozor over the mountains to Kiseljak. So, therefore, there were attempts made as early as late 1992 to build roads to assist with communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any such road ever reach the Vitez pocket during a war, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me change the subject now and ask: you've discussed the existence and organisation of the Central Bosnia operative zone on the part of the HVO. I would like to ask you: do you know what or which corps or corpus of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina operated on the same territory that you have described as the middle Bosnia or Central Bosnia operative zone of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was III Corps of the army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other corps that you know of the army of BiH that also operated within this same geographic area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is the I Corps, which was responsible for the Sarajevo area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or perhaps Disoko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was a VII Corps in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm only aware as far as corps, that there were only four in the Bosnian army. I Corps, Sarajevo. III Corps, base Zenica. II Corps, Tuzla and IV Corps in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said II Corps, Tuzla; III Corps Zenica; I Corps Sarajevo, possibly Disoko. So you are not aware of the VII Corps based in the Travnik area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. As I say, as far as I know the Bosnian army only had four corps, not seven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not familiar with the VI Corps based in the Fojnica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: VI Corps?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The VI Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you have testified that certain "attacks" occurred on certain dates. You have also shown us a number of photographs, many of which are disturbing, including photographs of damage or destroyed places of worship, particularly mosques or exclusively mosques. Is it your testimony that with respect to each location or village where you have show us a picture of a damaged or destroyed mosque, that that damage or destruction occurred on the date to which you have ascribed an HVO attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that's not my assertion. The damage to those mosques, apart from, I think, in Ahmici, where I think I am fairly accurate to say was on or about between 16th or 19th April, the damage to the other mosques occurred at dates which I don't know the timing of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the mosque in Busovaca damaged or destroyed; do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be surprised to learn that that mosque was damaged or destroyed in May of 1994, after the cease-fire between the HVO and the ABiH, after the Washington agreement and after the last date alleged in this indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would surprise you? Would you like to, and I'm sorry I don't have copies of this, your Honour, look at a Reuters news story, in which it is written -- this is dated June 20th, 1994. In fairness, your Honour, may I have a moment? I would like to show it to counsel, because I don't have copies of this. I am surprised by this testimony and I think in fairness I should show it to counsel before I ask the witness whether he's familiar with this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I would like this document to be given to the Prosecutor as well. Mr. Harmon, you don't have it? Mr. Leach, you don't have it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you like to take a few moments to examine it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, would you please give the Registrar the document, who will make a copy of it and then give it to the Prosecutor? Mr. Harmon, as soon as you have looked at it, as soon as you have it in your hands --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We can come back to this, your Honour. We can have copies made. I can continue with some other questions and we can come back to it. That will be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have described a number of events which you have stated occurred on April 16th or other dates in April or following months. Is it a fact that you yourself have no personal knowledge of any of these events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact in April, for example, of 1993, where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the United Kingdom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a police investigator, detective in the UK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So evidence that you testified about concerning events happening on particular days in 1993 and so forth is based on hearsay information that you have obtained from witness interviews or other documents, or from talking to other people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no personal knowledge of any attack by an HVO soldier or force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No personal knowledge of any detention of civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No personal knowledge of the particular dates on which any structure, whether mosque, residence or other, was damaged or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No personal knowledge as to who the owners of any destroyed structures or residences were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps apart from aggregate census data, no personal knowledge of the ethnicity or nationality of any such owners; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've made certain -- offered certain testimony concerning the ease of travel, particularly from the Hotel Vitez to surrounding areas as well as from the Kiseljak Barracks to surrounding areas. Would you agree that the ease of travel depends on the circumstances at the time, such as whether there exists a condition of peace time, or whether there exists a condition of wartime or a state of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would. I would agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is because in a state of war a vehicle -- it may not be safe to use a vehicle on a particular road or passageway; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That could be due to facts, for example, the fact that a section of the road such as the road between Bilalovic and Kacuni was in the hands of a warring party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or it could be due to the fact that a section of road was exposed to sniper fire from the opposing party; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or it could be due to the fact that a road or perhaps a mountainside or hillside may have been mined, thereby rendering it unsafe for travel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that on a particular date any of the roads or travels that you have described as being convenient and short were, in fact, possible during the war that was going on in connection with this case? Do you have any personal knowledge that on a particular date any of those roads or routes were, in fact, safe and passable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personal knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the HVO had any tanks or armoured vehicles at their disposal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe they may have, but I couldn't categorically state any factual figures on that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen any pictures of General Blaskic arriving at a meeting and jumping out of his own armoured personnel carrier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there was a UN-brokered meeting, he would arrive in a UN vehicle or UN armoured personnel carrier. Is that your general understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think the document, your Honour, has been copied and I would ask that it be marked as the next Defence exhibit in order and provided to the witness. I would direct counsel to the second page, second sentence of the first full paragraph, which is the sentence I intend to draw the witness' attention to, the sentence beginning: "Last month ...". Do you have this article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps the Tribunal could have a copy of this as well. (Handed.)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Why don't I read, your Honour, the introductory language, and that way we can obtain a translation? This exhibit, Mr. Leach, is titled "Croatia Waging War on History, June 20th, 1994. Text. “In the former Yugoslavia”, writes Robert Fisk, “whole cultures are being obliterated". This is a Reuters' story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, would you please put the document on the ELMO, so that the interpreters can have their work made easier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The specific by line -- if you would show that -- is the ELMO on, may I enquire? Mr. Leach, could you pull down the article so we can see the top and the by-line? You see the by-line is June 20th, 1994. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning the page, if you turn that page over to the back page of that same page, assuming your copy is a two-sided copy, and place the document again on the ELMO, so that the second -- the first full paragraph, at least the top portion, is visible. Let me read the first two sentences of that paragraph: "Nor has the destruction ended. In April Croat gunmen destroyed the mosque at Livno. Last month Croatian Bosnian forces demolished the minaret of the Busovaca mosque". Then it continues as to the destruction of a Catholic church. Would you agree that the reference "last month" to the destruction of the Busovaca mosque is a reference to the month prior to June 1994, namely May 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It appears to be so, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that surprising to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because, if true, then that mosque was destroyed after the period charged in this indictment; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If Exhibit 53, your Honour, could be placed -- I believe it needs to be placed on the easel. This should be an aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before we talk about 53, does this have to be put into the record as well? What will the number be? Mr. Hayman or Mr. Dubuisson, I'm talking about the Reuters' despatch.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is D/12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First I wanted to know whether Mr. Hayman wanted it to be put in the record. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, the second page, I think, is extraneous and can be removed. I think the article appears in toto in the first page. So the second page is not pertinent. It can be marked for identification. I don't feel strongly that it be admitted but I don't oppose its admission, if the other side would like it admitted, your Honour, but I would like it marked and made a part of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, your Honour. I didn't hear. I was in conversation with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I had a very simple question. I was asking for your approval for this to be put in as an exhibit under number D/12, 13? 12. The two-sided page, not the second page but the two-sided copy of the Reuters' despatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be D/12. Proceed please, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The next exhibit I would like to work with is 53, which is an aerial photograph. Perhaps that could be retrieved. Could you point out for us on this map, for example, the markings for Ahmici, Santici. I believe is Nadioci on this map? It is difficult for me to see from this distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, on this map Ahmici is here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. I have to consult my colleagues. (Pause.) Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Mr. Leach, could you point out the village of Nadioci? Is a particular location marked as Nadioci on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The weekend houses are marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village proper lies on the other side of the road to the north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then where have you marked the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again could you show us where the village of Nadioci ends and where the village of Ahmici begins?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again without being a local I would suggest that Ahmici ends below the pointer. Nadioci would begin above the pointer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact is the structures run together and they are quite approximate; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you are indicating these houses here as being part of Ahmici or Nadioci, I just couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, again, as in the case of the villages we were discussing to the north, north west of Kiseljak, there are no signs indicating where one village ends and the next begins; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there are not, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The houses are pretty much sprinkled across the hillside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are houses or farms sprinkled on the hillside, but I think, as in Gomionica and Behrici, you can distinguish one village from another. I think it would be more difficult to distinguish, for example, on this photograph where Ahmici ends and Santici begins, but for Ahmici and Nadioci, there is a distinct break in the ground that would assist in identifying one village from the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a ravine or some kind of depression?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not true or is it true with respect to Ahmici and I believe it's Pirici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean Pirici is a distinct smaller hamlet which is on the hill above Santici and Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that less than 1,000 metres from either one of those villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 1,000 metres would be accurate, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the method of organising governmental units for purpose of self-governance in Bosnia under the municipal level or opstina level, the next level down of government organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Limited knowledge. I'm not an expert at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, would you agree that these four villages in this area, Nadioci, Ahmici, Pirici and Santici were all part of one local community --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, the witness said he was not an expert. I don't see the point of this question if you knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Not being an expert -- with all due respect, your Honour, not being an expert doesn't mean he does not have any knowledge of it. I do not know if he has any knowledge of it. If he has none, he can certainly say: "I do not know".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Answer, Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether these four villages were part of a single community for government or self-government purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure that they were a single community as regards if one was -- if one was sat here as a Bosnian Muslim. As regards a Bosnian Croat, I seem to understand that the local HVO forces were under one command, which would include Nadioci, Pirici, Santici and Ahmici. How that mirrored for the Bosnian forces, I think that was given, because, for example, there were limited Muslims living in Nadioci. There was certainly a local group of the Muslims for the community of Ahmici that would have discussed civil defence, whereas for the HVO, from my understanding, it covered a larger area, which would be Nadioci down through Ahmici, Pirici and Santici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One moment, your Honour. (Pause.)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I'm referring to a system of self-governance as it existed before the war. Do you have any knowledge of that scheme with respect to these four villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, your Honours, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May I approach, your Honour, and point out some terrain on the map for my next question? First I would like to point out the main road from Vitez towards the Busovaca T-junction and ask you if, in fact, I'm accurately identifying the main road (indicating)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's accurate, your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that the road lies in a valley (indicating)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the south of the valley there are steep hills raising?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And similarly there are hills to the north of the valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the villages we have been discussing -- I'm sorry. Let's take a moment and ... thank you, Mr. Dubuisson. The villages we have been discussing, they generally line the hillsides to the north of the valley which contains both the road and the river. Would you agree the hillside which I'm indicating now to the north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For example, the village of Santici and a sizeable portion of Ahmici lie next to the road. As you drive along the road, if a house was within 15, 20 metres of that road, with a garden in front of it, that would be part of the village. So a portion of the village, for example, Santici, the majority of that village is on flat ground. For example, Ahmici, because it's a village with perhaps three distinct area, some of it is on flat ground and then the upper part of the village is on high ground. The village of Pirici is solely on high ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, to clarify then, with respect to Santici, Ahmici and Nadioci, some of the houses or structures in those villages run all the way down to the road; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now do you know that, in fact, this road was the subject of extreme and bitter fighting between Croat and Muslim forces in this area in, for example, late 1993 and early 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, your Honours, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at one point cut this road as well, creating two enclaves within the Vitez enclave; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether of the destroyed houses near the road, again do you know when that destruction occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think some other witnesses will be able to tell which buildings were destroyed at what time. I don't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you cannot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have personal knowledge of that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in taking photos of the destroyed homes and structures that you have helped document for us all, did you look for any fortification in the areas of any apparent conflicts? By fortification I mean trenches, bunkers, fox holes, that type of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you look? In and around which villages did you look for fortification?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our mission, when we were taking photography was limited to where we were allowed to travel. For example, there is a small location near to Pirici which, when I visited there, was being reinhabited by Bosnian Muslims. They described to me that the village had been attacked or that location had been attacked by the HVO on 16th April, and then they showed me some trenches and what appeared to be a command post, which would link one trench system to another and indicated that that was HVO trench positions, which was just below a ridge line, but we were very restricted in our ability to investigate any trench positions. Particularly I distinctly remember seeing mines at the side of the road in the grass in that location. It is quite surprising to see people rebuilding their homes when there are mines next to the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take any pictures of any fortification?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look for any fortification that would indicate defensive fortification approximate to these villages, not a confrontation line later in the war, but defensive fortification approximate to Pirici, Ahmici and Santici and so forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not a soldier so I wouldn't know. If I saw a trench, I would take a photograph, if possible, of a trench or associated structure, but I'm simply not qualified to say when that structure was built, when the trench was dug, whether it was dug for the purposes of defence, whether it was dug for the purposes of offence, whether it was -- whether that positioning of that trench could serve both purposes. I'm just not a military man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have any of those photographs been provided to the Defence, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll reserve that point, your Honour, for a later hearing. Perhaps, your Honour, while I ask some more questions about this exhibit, Mr. Dubuisson could assist and see if he can locate the aerial photograph of the town of Vitez. With respect to these maps, is this exhibit one of the maps provided by the UK Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you gave various dates on which you believed these photographs were taken. Do you know those dates from your own personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not from my personal knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They have been provided to you by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that it's very important that the Tribunal know the date of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because if they were taken on a different date before or after the war, they may reflect the existence of structures or the non-existence of structures and be misleading. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know were these maps obtained from the Ministry of Defence for use for this purpose, to be used and presented as evidence in the trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We asked for these maps, those photographs. What use they would be put to at the time, certainly for trial ... they have since been put to use during trial. Whether that was the initial objective, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of these aerial photographs were shown to the Defence prior to being presented and moved into evidence at the trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recall showing yourself one some months ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any of the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You believe they were not shown to the Defence prior to being moved for admission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a few more questions about this subject and I'm not asking you to reveal any sensitive or confidential data, so please answer carefully. Without telling us which, do you know whether these photographs were taken as a result of over flight photography or satellite photography and I'm not asking for you to specify but I'm asking you do you know whether it was one or the other?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to object, your Honour. I think that question is improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. First, I would like Mr. Hayman to finish his question and then I can deal with your objection. Have you completed -- first of all I would like to ask you, Mr. Hayman, whether you have completed your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would object, your Honour, to the means in which this photograph was taken. I don't believe that is a proper question to be asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I can explain my purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What was your purpose, Mr. Hayman, the reasons you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We've heard, for example, that at least there's a possibility the mosque in Busovaca was not destroyed until May of 1994. If these photographs were taken as part of a regular series, there may be other maps, perhaps at monthly intervals or quarterly intervals, that could help us learn, all of us when particular structures were destroyed and so forth. That's more likely to be the case if they are satellite photos taken during regular over flights of the region. On the other hand, if a special airplane, aerial photography was undertaken, a one-time mission, then that possibility would not exist. I'm simply trying to identify the relevant issues under Rule 70. I'm not trying to extract any sensitive information from this witness. I'm not asking him whether it was satellite or over flight. I'm just asking him whether he knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, as Rule 70, you know that you can only reveal the source with the consent of the person or entity who supplied them to you. I suppose you have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct, your Honour. That is one of the bases of my objections. The other is, your Honour, these photographs have been tendered for purposes of showing various relationships of villages and the like. Mr. Leach has testified that these exhibits accurately depict the relationships and the physical characteristics as in each of these exhibits. The provider has not authorised us to reveal the nature of the source of these photographs, how they were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but, Mr. Harmon, you put me into somewhat of a paradoxical situation. You are showing these maps. You have the consent of the person or entities who provided them. You have just said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Therefore, it's obvious that you are in a situation where the Defence is using them and it seems in order to use them he needs to ask a certain number of questions. Now if your investigator and witness considers that he cannot answer some of the questions, he just will not answer and the Tribunal will take the consequences from that, which it considers appropriate to take. You took the initiative of showing these maps. You remember that the Defence raised objections of principle and I can also say to the Defence that it's using these maps. Therefore some of the objections raised by the Defence can no longer be made. However, since the maps are there, they were accepted as evidence and the Tribunal must be sure that they are covered by Rule 70B, and my conclusion is that if the investigator cannot answer some of the questions, then he will not answer. All of this will be put in the transcript, and the Tribunal will draw the consequences that it has to draw from that. I think that you can now proceed, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We will simply take -- I take it, your Honour, to that question the witness declines to answer on grounds of Rule 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's fair to say that the witness declines to answer that question because he is not authorised by the provider to provide the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That's fine. I just wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, you can't dictate the answer, Mr. Prosecutor. He knows what he's going to answer. Let the Presiding Judge ask the witness to answer the way he wants. It's not Mr. Leach's answer through Mr. Harmon. Mr. Hayman asked a question. Mr. Leach, would you like to answer the question? First of all, going back to Mr. Hayman, would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Without telling us, Mr. Leach, whether this was satellite or aerial imagery, that's over flight imagery, can you tell us whether you know which of those categories was the source of this photography?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have no knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you turn on your microphone, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us also you have no personal knowledge of the dates on which this or any other aerial photograph were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The dates I have provided in my testimony were, I believe, the accurate dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were provided to you by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to identify that person to us or is that something you cannot do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I enquire, your Honour, whether Mr. Dubuisson has located an aerial photograph of the town of Vitez? If he has, I would ask that it be placed on the easel. In terms of this Rule 70 question, your Honour, I suggest that it be reserved and it can be discussed at a future time convenient to the court, the potential implications of this type of situation. I don't feel any need to go into it further here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: However, I would like to point out, Mr. Hayman, that you are now using this evidence. Therefore, you cannot at the same time challenge the principle of protection and use the evidence as part of your strategy. Therefore, if you desire at another point in the proceedings, if you wish to ask questions, the Tribunal will note the questions, but for the time being the Tribunal notes that you yourself are using this evidence for the Defence of your client. Are we agreed on that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I have asked the witness about it, but I would also submit I should not be required to put all of my eggs in one basket; in other words, I shouldn't be required to abstain from asking any questions in the hope the exhibit is excluded under Rule 70 and then if it is not, I have foregone any cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We did not understand one another. I don't think I expressed myself correctly. One way or another this evidence -- there are two questions that arise. There is a principle to know whether it is covered by Rule 70. On that point, since the day before yesterday, you made some comments. One way or another you have just repeated that. We have noted it. If you want to go back to what you said before, you can. But the second point is that apparently you need for the Defence of your client, you need to use this evidence. However, I am simply noting that. Now perhaps we can put the Vitez photo up, but even before we do that, perhaps we should take a break and resume at 11.35. The court stands adjourned. (11.15 am) (Short break) (11.35 am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The session is resumed. Can we have the accused in, please? (Accused re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, do you think that you'll be finished by 1 o'clock?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will be finished in ten minutes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perfect. I ask this question so that we would know how much time would be needed, because the judges have some questions to ask as well, and we need it for the organisation of our work. Mr. Dubuisson, let's be sure that we have the proper maps being displayed. All right. Proceed please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, we have here on the easel, Exhibit 45, an aerial photograph principally of the Vitez town area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You previously testified that the Hotel Vitez lies in the valley floor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's in the centre of Vitez. I do not know if I used the phrase "valley floor". I may have done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the town of Vitez lie in the valley floor of the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, can you see -- is this the river flowing here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That appears to be the river, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to direct your attention to the Hotel Vitez on this map and perhaps, if it's possible, your Honour, the camera can zoom in a bit, because I know this map is difficult to see from the distance at which the court sits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I do not know whether the camera will be able to do it. It's trying to facilitate your work, Mr. Hayman. Now, Mr. Leach, can see the map and the judges can see it as well, as well as seeing the Hotel Vitez. I do not know if the camera can actually do all of that but let's try. Go ahead fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree the location mark A, Hotel Vitez, is the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that looking across in this manner towards the river, that that's roughly a northerly direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now do you know where the front door of the Hotel Vitez is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would describe the front door as being the main entrance, which is on the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The main road being this road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Running in an east-west direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And there's a small lawn with some trees in front of it and it has, say, a glass domed canopy in front of the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you step in front of the Hotel Vitez and look across the road, what do you see, what I'm pointing at with this pen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I can see -- there's a building opposite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a gas station, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The gas station is further down the road to the south -- to the west possibly. I think opposite the Hotel Vitez may be the municipal buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there a number of buildings across the street to the north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you look out from the front of the hotel, you see those buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if you look to the right in an easterly direction from the front of the hotel, you see another building, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the building marked C on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many floors is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The PTT building?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure, maybe two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is at least two or three floors, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if you look where my pen is, I'm showing an arc to the east and the north. Would you agree with a small path through the PTT building and the building immediately to the north, basically all you would see to the north and the east of the entrance to the Hotel Vitez are these other buildings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the ground level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you look -- if you were to look to the north, north west from the entrance of the Hotel Vitez, looking up the hill in the manner I'm indicating (indicating) what would you see up here or beyond?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't, first of all, describe that as a hill but you would see open ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would see open ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The hill is probably 2 kms further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are any of the villages you have described as having been attacked, are they located in this open ground area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they're not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you taken any pictures that would depict exactly what you can see from the front entrance of the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you've identified by the letter E the front line boundary between Vitez and Stari Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that if one were to come out on to the front steps of the Hotel Vitez, you would be exposed, at least potentially, to sniper fire from Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could only speculate. Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your review of the materials in your files, can you tell this court whether or not individuals were killed on the front steps of the Hotel Vitez during the war from gunfire from Stari Vitez, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a rear entrance to the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand so but I do not know where it is on the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever stood at the rear entrance and looked to see what you can see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that from this map, if the rear entrance is at the back, that is the south side of the hotel, that there appears to be a large structure immediately to the south?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now when you were a police detective or inspector in the United Kingdom would you work with the Prosecutor to identify and collect the evidence relevant to a potential prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Subject to the nature of the investigation. Normally one would conduct an investigation somewhat independently. The more complex the investigation is, a senior police officer higher rank than me may ask or request the Crown Prosecution Service for the immediate involvement of a prosecuting counsel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your role would include identifying potential witnesses; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And obtaining information from them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you've obviously undertaken a vast effort here to collect information and potential evidence to bring it to this Tribunal. Have you yourself interviewed witnesses in Bosnia and Herzegovina in connection with this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now without revealing the identity of any such witnesses, can you tell us how those witnesses were selected for interview? Who identified them?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm reluctant to intervene again, but this is clearly beyond the scope of the direct examination. Mr. Leach's direct examination was limited to the introduction of physical evidence, not into the methods of investigation and enquiry. I would, therefore, object to this line of enquiry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: May I be heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Had he limited himself to physical evidence, the objection might well be well taken but he also commented on events and other information that could only have come from witness information, and therefore I think we are entitled to ask a few questions about the process by way the investigators have collected, if in fact they have done the collection themselves, and brought evidence to the court. (Pause.)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Oui. There is a lot of practice here and I appreciate the opinions of my colleagues. Mr. Hayman, what we are requesting from you is that you always remain as part of your strategy, of course, but during a cross-examination in respect of what the investigators said, but having said that we do not sustain the Prosecutor's objection, and we will allow Mr. Hayman to go on with his question, but we will be very vigilant that the limits or the borders of cross-examination not be exceeded. You may proceed, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I have about five questions that I hope to ask concerning the process of collecting evidence. The question I think I had posed, Mr. Leach, was: have you interviewed witnesses in Bosnia and Herzegovina, without identifying any identities or any information that would tend to identify any such witnesses? Have you had the occasion to conduct or participate in such interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, again without identifying any witnesses or other personnel, were those witnesses initially selected for interview in connection with this matter by you and your staff or by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We collected initially information provided through the Bosnian government authorities. In certain cases they had taken statements from witnesses. Those statements would either be translated fully or summarily, subject to the limitations on the translation unit here. We then in the Office of the Prosecutor and the investigative team would select witnesses and thereafter identify other witnesses that we would want to locate to interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the initial batch of material that came to you and your office were selected by this state organ of Bosnia and Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not just one organ; more than one source.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it principally come from one source within that government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the entity known as AID?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And AID has a State security or intelligence function on behalf of the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know on those occasions where you participated in an interview, do you know how the witness came to be notified or asked to come to the interview? Were they picked up by the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they brought to a police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'd rather not discuss where interviews took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. They were brought to a location by the police force of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there you would have the chance to meet with the individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, we are going into quite a bit of detail on methods of operation. I would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Absolutely. Objection sustained. Please change questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I move on, your Honour. I would ask that Mr. Leach be instructed to remain on call to testify in the Defence case, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, you will remain available to the Tribunal, should the Defence need for you to reappear. Mr. Hayman, have you finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I have one more small area of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Leach, on Exhibit 45, does that exhibit depict the UNPROFOR base at Nova Bila, the so-called Brit Bat base?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what direction it would lie from this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll unplug my microphone, your Honours, and show you (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to get to the UNPROFOR Brit Bat base, you would follow the road that passes -- you would follow the main road up in a north west, north-westerly direction towards Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Travnik and you would go towards Novi Travnik, but one would turn left at a T-junction to go to Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how far was the Brit Bat base from, say, the Hotel Vitez? Are you able to tell us that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's 4.3 kms and takes about 6 minutes by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far then would the Brit Bat base have been from the village of Ahmici? I am sorry to have to ask you to perform mathematical calculation, but I must, and I'm sure you can do it better than I would?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 7-8.5 kms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read the book "Broken lives"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once -- twice but a long time ago but yes, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the commander of the British UNPROFOR forces at the time in April, this period in April, mid-April 1993, was Colonel Stewart; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Robert Stewart, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember from his book when he first learned of the massacre in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20th or 21st April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was not on the 16th; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think it was, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was not on the 17th; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20th or 21st April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has already answered the question and I would object to continued questions on that particular line of enquiry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that we have already set the case law here. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So your best recollection, it was four or five days after the massacre occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I could confirm it, if I looked at the book, but possibly three, four, five days. It's over one year since I've read the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is the question I was going ask you. You did read the book, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour. Thank you, Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon? Re-examination by Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I have two areas of enquiry.
